To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MovieFiber model, which combines language, static (two dimensional) and moving (three dimensional) visual features, performs the best on the MovieFib dataset.

(1) the MovieFIB dataset provides a useful benchmark for evaluating models for video question answering, and (2) the best model for the task uses a combination of 2D and (3D) video information, and performs significantly worse than human level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a dataset and exploring the models for understanding video data through fill-in-the-blanks questions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a dataset that can be used for evaluating video models and provide an in-depth analysis of the dataset and models.
the MovieFib dataset is a simple yet challenging dataset for video understanding, which is based on descriptive video annotation.
we present a new video understanding benchmark, and perform a thorough analysis of different model types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the current state-of-the-art model on the MovieFib task is still very far from human performance.
the task is not solvabe with language model alone and that the best result is obtained by combining 2D+3D visual features.
the task of answering questions about videos is a challenging one, which requires a combination of language, static and moving visual features.
